title: Drawer Grid
brief: A three-compartment organizer, sized to your drawer. Compare three widths, keep the pocket spaces and floor intact, then take the editable design and individual STLs to your slicer.
assumptions: Example dimensions, not measurements of your drawer: confirm clear internal width, depth and usable height before printing.
Allow additional clearance for drawer taper, seams and printer dimensional error; the outside dimensions are the requested part envelope.
Dry desk/craft storage only. No food contact, load-bearing or liquid-tightness claim.
assembly: Print a small fit sample or the narrow version first; measure the finished result.
Use one chosen size per drawer. The three variants are alternatives, not a three-piece assembly.

variants.label: Compact
notes: 150 mm wide for a smaller drawer or a second organizer beside it.

variants.label: Everyday
notes: 180 mm wide. Confirm the real drawer allows clearance around the part.

variants.label: Wide
notes: 210 mm wide; each compartment is wider while the wall and floor targets stay unchanged.

parts.label: Compartment tray
notes: Open top, continuous floor, full-height dividers. The top and front sections reveal all three pockets.
Print with the continuous floor on the bed. Review slicing, material, shrinkage and edge lifting for your machine.

checks.label: Outside dimensions match the saved drawer envelope
Every compartment has the required clear interior
The specified floor is present under the entire tray
Every interior divider retains the requested material
The back wall is continuous above the floor

notes: Declared example process: 0.4 mm nozzle, 235 × 235 × 250 mm printer. Change these to your machine.
The checks do not generate G-code or validate supports, extrusion settings or actual layer bonding.
